title: Java Collections: Deduplicate in Encounter Order
contract: Return unique integers in order of first appearance. Compare ArrayList membership with LinkedHashSet.
brute: List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>();for(int x:a){if(!out.contains(x))out.add(x);emit("Linear membership scan","value",x,"unique",out);}return out;
optimal: Set<Integer> seen=new LinkedHashSet<>();for(int x:a){seen.add(x);emit("Hash membership with encounter ordering","value",x,"unique",seen);}return new ArrayList<>(seen);
reasoning: ArrayList offers indexed storage, but contains scans existing values.
LinkedHashSet combines hash membership with insertion order; HashSet alone does not promise that order.
Choose by required operations, ordering, and equality semantics. Mutable keys whose hashCode changes break lookup assumptions. These collections do not provide automatic thread safety.
